principles: Deterministic recall sources must anchor model-proposed semantic expansion.
Every candidate and full read must have an auditable reason and evidence binding.
Efficiency improvements may narrow default reads but must not lower the review quality floor.
drivers: Preserve semantic recall across legacy terminology
Provide machine-checkable routing and escalation evidence

options.name: A: Hybrid deterministic plus multi-host keyword routing
cons: Requires shared schemas and routing metrics

options.name: C: Always read the entire corpus
cons: Does not prove what was actually read

chosen: A: Hybrid deterministic plus multi-host keyword routing
rationale: A preserves deterministic anchors while using host diversity for semantic recall and keeps every selection, omission, and escalation mechanically auditable.

preMortem.scenario: All hosts repeat the same modern terminology and miss a legacy synonym
preMortem.trigger: Candidate set is built only from host proposals
preMortem.mitigation: Require deterministic story/touchpoint/config seeds, filename enumeration, and lexical expansion before host union

preMortem.scenario: Candidate cap hides a relevant lower-ranked document
preMortem.trigger: Ranking scores cluster near the cutoff or hosts disagree
preMortem.mitigation: Treat ambiguity/cutoff ties/disagreement as escalation triggers and record scanEscalationReason

preMortem.scenario: The plan claims quality preservation without a baseline
preMortem.mitigation: Require golden corpus recall fixtures and before/after defect-equivalence comparisons

preMortem.scenario: Host proposals are mistaken for gate evidence
preMortem.trigger: Proposal provenance is not separated from reviewer reads
preMortem.consequence: Unverified model output satisfies scope claims
preMortem.mitigation: Mark proposals advisory and require signed scope_check_save plus mechanical readManifest/read-log reconciliation
